resources.string:
Getting started
Kansen helps you listen to and identify Hindustani swaras.
• Scales: explore and play notes.
• Training: practise identifying scales and swaras.
• Use the back arrow to return.

Language
Marathi is the default. Use the language button at the top to switch between Marathi and English. Your choice is remembered.

Instrument
• Choose Harmonium or Pure tone on the home page. Harmonium is the default.
• Your choice is remembered across app restarts and applies to all notes, exercises and saptak comparisons.
• Instrument sounds are synthesized from measurements of reference samples: their resonances, changes in tone and noise. The recordings themselves are not played. Pure tone has no added harmonics.
• All instruments use the same tuning. Harmonium and Pure tone fade in over 1 second and sustain while held.

Scales and keys
Choose from 12 scales: seven white and five black. The circle beside each scale indicates its tonic key colour.
• In Madhya saptak, White 1 starts at C4. The scales rise in semitone steps through B4.
• Select Mandra, Madhya or Taar saptak from the dropdown. Mandra is one octave below Madhya; Taar is one octave above.
• Each harmonium layout has 12 swaras plus the next, higher Sa. Komal and tivra notes are labelled explicitly.
• Hold a key to hear it continuously; release it to stop. Its swara name and frequency in Hz appear below while held.
• Tap Sa beside the scale name to hear its reference Sa for 3 seconds.

Scale identification
A scale is selected at random.
• Play: hear its Sa for 3 seconds. Play repeats the same Sa until you refresh.
• Refresh: choose a different scale and hide the answer.
• Reveal / Hide: show or conceal the scale below the buttons.

Note identification
Choose a scale from the dropdown, or choose Random. The exercise uses the 12 swaras within one octave.
• Play: hear the reference Sa for 3 seconds, followed by a random swara from that scale for 3 seconds.
• Refresh: choose a different swara. With Random selected, the scale changes too.
• Reveal / Hide: show or conceal both the swara and its scale.
• Play repeats the same pair until you refresh or change the dropdown selection. Changing the selection starts a new question.

Saptak identification
• Choose a scale from the dropdown.
• Play: hear one random swara in a random saptak within your chosen scale for 3 seconds.
• Refresh: choose a new swara and random saptak, keeping your selected scale. Play repeats the same note until you refresh or change the scale.
• Reveal / Hide: show or conceal the selected saptak, scale and swara.
• After revealing, use the two buttons below to hear the same swara in the other two saptaks, for 3 seconds each. The selected scale and original question stay unchanged.
• The selected scale fixes the reference Madhya Sa: White 1 uses C4, rising through White 7 at B4. Identify the swara and saptak relative to that reference.
• Scale and note identification exercises continue to use Madhya saptak.

Playback and countdown
• 1-second fade-in: Harmonium and Pure tone start silent and gradually reach full volume during their first second.
• The fade-in is included in the 3-second playback duration. These held tones fade in once.
• Training shows a shrinking ring with a 3–2–1 countdown. In note identification, the countdown restarts for the second sound.
• Dismissing the countdown popup stops playback.
• Playback ends with a brief 20 ms fade-out to avoid a click.

Sound and tuning
• Use your device’s media volume to adjust loudness.
• The sounds are synthesized, not recordings of real instruments.
• Tuning uses 12-tone equal temperament with A4 = 440 Hz, like an equal-tempered harmonium. Raga-specific shruti adjustments are not modelled.
• The app works offline. Check your answers yourself: the exercises do not listen to or grade your singing.

Sound references
• Harmonium: Donya Quick. Reference excerpts prepared by Nicholaus P. Brosowsky / tonejs-instruments (CC BY 3.0): github.com/nbrosowsky/tonejs-instruments
• References were analyzed into spectral models and retuned for synthesis. No endorsement is implied. Licenses: creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/
